lastText: OHLLAGEBERICHTHome19141915191619171918-3MANPOWER-3MUNITIONS-2HOME FRONTXI.1918The RequestThe army in the west is not broken in the sense the word is used in staff colleges. It is retreating in order, on ground it still holds, in front of an enemy it can still hurt. What has gone is the possibility of any outcome except a worse one later. The Americans came late and in smaller numbers, and it made a difference of months rather than of outcome. The request goes forward from the Supreme Command. It is a military judgment, made by soldiers, and within a few years a great many people who were in this building will say it was made by someone else.Settled recordChief of the General Staff at the close: Hindenburg. The war ends on the eleventh of November. Lorraine, August 1914: reinforced. The Marne: delegated forward under plenipotentiary authority. The Meuse: fought as the directive was written. The submarines: held under prize rules. Weight of effort after the Marne: held in the west. Posture for 1917: continued offensive effort. American entry: deferred. Brest-Litovsk: maximal settlement, divisions retained in garrison. Spring 1918: breakthrough taken as the objective. September 1918: requested through a new civil government.Return to file
